subject: Post-call: Latency vs Cost — pricing & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@fintechai.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom@fintechai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + pricing worksheet attached

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — great discussion and appreciate the clarity on the three core use cases you described (real-time chat assistant, nightly batch summaries, and an internal reranking service). Quick recap + next steps from my side: 

- Key asks we captured from FinTechAI: monthly token volumes by use case, target latency SLOs (p50/p95), and an initial target budget range for unit economics (target $/1M tokens).
- Suggested immediate next step: 2-week pilot focused on chat assistant to validate latency and unit costs under production-like traffic.
- I've attached our latest pricing worksheet (Redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf) and a short SLA draft for your procurement team (SLA-draft.docx).

High-level pricing guidance we discussed on call (see attached sheet for detail):
- Hosted (low friction): good for fast time-to-value, flexible usage. Typical unit economics: ~$150-300 per 1M tokens depending on model and streaming vs batch.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): better $/1M at predictable throughput; with batching/quantization you can get down to ~$60-120 per 1M tokens for non-low-latency workloads.
- Private/VPC: for regulated workflows, pricing varies based on infra; often treated as contracted pricing.

Latency vs cost trade-off notes (from call):
- Aggressive batching (larger batch windows) improves $/token but increases tail latency and risk for p95-sensitive workloads.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for end users but can increase compute overhead depending on model and token churn.
- We can tune batching thresholds, CPU/GPU assignment, and KV cache settings per route to meet SLOs.

Action items: 
1) Samantha/Tom: share expected monthly token volumes by use case and a target budget range (ballpark is fine).
2) Rishi/Dev: prepare a 2-week pilot plan and estimate pilot budget and runbook.
3) Marissa: follow up with any clarifying questions and finalize pilot dates.

Thanks — I'll stand up the pricing pilot plan once we have volumes.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing worksheet attached

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes (initial estimate, month 1): chat assistant 3M tokens/mo, batch summaries 8M tokens/mo (nightly), reranking 2M tokens/mo => ~13M tokens/mo total. We expect 2-3x growth over the next 6-12 months if success metrics look good.
- Latency SLOs: for chat assistant p50 ~150ms, p95 ideally <350ms. Batch summaries can be best-effort (latency not critical). Reranking needs p95 <500ms.
- Budget: we'd like to target roughly $100-150 per 1M tokens for the pilot and go-to-prod if feasible. Procurement will need a clear pilot cost estimate.

Questions: 
1) Given our p95 targets, do you recommend Hosted (top tier) or Dedicated?
2) How much of a delta should we expect between streaming vs batch for costs?

If you can provide a two-tier estimate (pilot expected spend and steady-state expected monthly spend at 13M tokens with 2x headroom), that would help us get procurement aligned.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Product | FinTechAI
samantha@fintechai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@fintechai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing worksheet attached

Samantha — great, that volume/budget context is super helpful. Quick answers and an initial estimate below.

1) Hosted vs Dedicated recommendation (given your p95 targets):
- Hosted (higher-tier, optimized routes + streaming): easiest for pilot and can meet p95 <350ms for many models if you pick a low-latency model variant. Expect ~10-25% premium over dedicated because of multi-tenant overhead and dynamic scaling.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): preferred for predictable cost at scale. With tuned batching & quantization for reranking and batch summaries you can hit $60-120 per 1M tokens for those workloads — but chat assistant with strict p95 will need some dedicated low-latency nodes (higher unit cost) or a mixed routing policy.

2) Streaming vs batch cost delta (rule-of-thumb):
- Streaming: +10-40% compute overhead versus batch, depending on token churn and model (short-turn chat benefits more). It reduces perceived latency for end users.
- Aggressive batching: reduces $/token significantly (15-50% depending on model/hardware) but increases tail latency — not suitable for chat p95 <350ms unless you use small batch windows.

Initial pricing estimate for pilot (2 weeks) based on 3M chat tokens/mo scaled down to two weeks of traffic and 13M total monthly (pro-rated):
- Pilot (2 weeks of production-like traffic, focused on chat): estimate $2,200-3,500 total. This assumes hosted low-latency route with streaming enabled and baseline model.
- Steady-state at 13M tokens/mo (mixed workload):
  - Scenario A (hosted, low-latency priority for chat): ~$130 per 1M tokens => ~$1,690/mo (13M)
  - Scenario B (dedicated mix, batch summaries optimized): ~$85 per 1M tokens weighted avg => ~$1,105/mo (13M)

Notes: these are starting estimates — exact numbers depend on model choice, average sequence length, and how much of the traffic benefits from batching/quantization. I'll ask Dev to prepare a short cost model spreadsheet that breaks down token-level compute, batching assumptions, and expected $/1M under different batch sizes.

Next steps (what we'll deliver by end of day tomorrow):
- Dev: pilot runbook + cost model spreadsheet for 13M tokens with two scenarios.
- Rishi: suggested commercial terms for a 3-month pilot (including a one-time credit option).
- Samantha: confirm preferred pilot window and whether procurement needs an MSA or can accept the SLA draft for initial work.

If you want, we can also set up a short technical call with our infra team to pick batch/window targets and streaming configs.

Best,
Marissa

- FinTechAI target of $100-150 per 1M is reasonable for hosted; we should present the pilot at the mid-point and offer a clear path to ~$80/1M in dedicated if they commit to a 6-12 month reserved CAP.
- Recommend offering a one-time pilot credit of up to $1,500 to reduce friction. If pilot runs well, propose an initial 3-month commitment at a blended rate (e.g., $110/1M) then re-evaluate pricing at scale.
- Dev: include two cost curves in the spreadsheet: (1) per-1M at different batch sizes/sequence lengths, (2) per-1M for streaming vs batch for chat. Keep the pilot conservative on batching (small batch windows) to guarantee p95.

I'll draft the pilot commercial terms (simple SOW + credit) and attach to the SLA draft.
